briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for September 30, 2026. Based on the 152 climate-related news items collected today, we will provide an in-depth analysis of key trends and pressing challenges.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis Warnings and Pressing Challenges
sections.content: The most urgent news in today's briefing is the warning about the deepening climate crisis and its widespread impacts. Domestically, ecosystem changes are becoming a reality, such as the disappearance of 'autumn salted shrimp' [2] and the projection that winter will vanish in Jeju Island in 55 years [10]. Farmers are also experiencing crop wilting and premature abandonment of cultivation [25]. Notably, despite achieving the 2025 national greenhouse gas reduction target, the pace of reduction has slowed for three consecutive years, and net emissions have increased, signaling a warning for Korea's carbon reduction efforts [24, 32, 36, 89]. Internationally, climate change is linked to rising food prices [124, 131], worsening skin diseases [130, 140], and the realization of ecological threats such as killer mosquitoes and rabid bats [128]. There are also concerns that Asian corporate boards risk overlooking 'human health,' a significant cost of climate change [127]. Furthermore, challenges in implementing climate response policies are being detected in various areas, including the expectation that Europe may postpone methane regulations due to an energy crisis originating from the Middle East [3], concerns about missing the 'golden time' for renewable energy transition [115], and the challenge of securing profitability for offshore wind power [120].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Response Efforts and Policy Progress
sections.content: Domestically, various educational and policy efforts to address climate change are actively underway. The Korea Climate Change Research Institute is strengthening international cooperation by conducting training to enhance greenhouse gas verification capabilities in Indonesia [1, 7]. Local education offices are also holding climate change and ecological transition education workshops to explore practical applications [11, 21, 23, 30]. Amidst calls for 'climate audits' to verify climate change response policies and projects [6, 34, 55], Incheon City held an interim report meeting for the establishment of its 4th Climate Crisis Adaptation Plan [22]. In local communities, 31 basic local government carbon neutrality centers have launched a consultative body, striving to expand carbon neutrality practices [39, 48, 53, 54, 61, 67, 86]. Activities such as Seogwipo City's 'Carbon Neutrality Leaders' [51, 69, 74] and various local governments' carbon-neutral lifestyle practice campaigns [27, 33, 40, 62, 63, 64, 70, 75, 77, 78, 80, 82, 83, 84, 85, 87, 92] are gaining momentum. Furthermore, tangible results are emerging, with Gyeongsangbuk-do accelerating its 2050 carbon neutrality implementation [57] and Pyeongtaek City achieving 90% of its greenhouse gas reduction target for the first half of the year [66, 90].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Grid Innovation
sections.content: Accelerating renewable energy transition and grid innovation is one of today's key positive developments. The government has announced plans to innovate the power grid system to accommodate over 100 GW of renewable energy by 2030, securing an additional 78 GW of grid capacity for this purpose [94, 98, 100, 104, 106, 109, 110]. Notably, renewable energy grid regulations in the Honam region have been lifted after two years [108], with new connections set to resume from January next year [112, 113]. President Lee also announced plans to expand the power grid to enable local consumption of Honam's renewable energy [93]. Domestically, a 94.7 MW floating solar power project at Soyanggang Dam has broken ground [119, 122], and LH achieved nearly 80% energy self-sufficiency with new and renewable energy, earning an award at an international academic conference [114]. Internationally, India is also accelerating its energy transition towards carbon neutrality by approving a $19 billion renewable energy program [99, 152].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Change Awareness and Response Trends
sections.content: In the international community, deepening awareness of climate change is accompanied by diverse levels of response efforts. Public awareness is growing, with questions recently being raised about whether direct experience with climate phenomena has changed perceptions of the climate crisis [125]. Younger generations are actively developing climate change response ideas and leading efforts for the future [126, 138, 143]. Concrete action plans are being pursued, such as the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) approving a new action plan on health and climate change [133], and U.S. cities investing to protect residents from climate change [123]. However, the warning that Asian corporate boards risk overlooking 'human health,' the greatest cost of climate change [127], and reports that climate change is linked to worsening skin health in over 40% of countries worldwide [130, 140] still highlight the serious challenges faced by the international community. Dr. Moses Wetang'ula, Speaker of the African Parliament, emphasized the importance of a united response, urging punishment for climate polluters and self-financing of climate action in Africa [141].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severe reality of the climate crisis while simultaneously shedding light on various domestic and international efforts to overcome it. Amidst the immediate threats, we have once again confirmed the importance of renewable energy transition, education, and international cooperation. This is a time that demands continuous attention and action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
